incidents.victim: Telecom carriers and subscribers (Taiwan primarily, 6 countries)
incidents.vector: Backdoors planted in telecom infrastructure run malicious SS7 and Diameter signaling commands to collect device data and track subscriber locations.
incidents.impact: Enabled interception of calls and SMS traffic and covert tracking of select high-value individuals, including political figures and government officials, across telcos in six countries since early 2025.

incidents.victim: Managed service providers and their customers (~400 partner environments, 48+ organizations confirmed affected)
incidents.vector: Abuse of the RMM+ third-party ScreenConnect extension (a blank-passphrase authentication flaw) and likely compromised operator credentials to push commands that install a rogue ScreenConnect client and the SCKit toolkit.
incidents.impact: Attackers created persistent backdoors, hijacked technician sessions via the toolkit's RelayTrap component, and spread malware across managed endpoints within 90 minutes at affected MSPs; ConnectWise disabled RMM+ across roughly 400 partner environments and urged credential resets.

incidents.victim: U.S. air traffic control communications network
incidents.vector: Cause not yet confirmed; a communications failure at air traffic control centers triggered a nationwide ground stop. DHS says it has no evidence of a cyberattack or rogue AI agent, but the FBI is investigating.
incidents.impact: Roughly 10,000 flights were canceled in the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since September 11, 2001; full recovery was expected to take days.

incidents.victim: Cryptocurrency/Web3 individuals and open-source software maintainers
incidents.vector: Deepfake-enabled video-call social engineering ('FaceStealer') lures targets into fake meetings, plays a prerecorded video of a trusted contact, then tricks the target into installing malware via a fake technical-error prompt.
incidents.impact: More than $400 million in cryptocurrency was stolen over 18 months; hackers also compromised an open-source JavaScript library maintainer to plant malicious dependencies. DOJ and the FBI seized cloud infrastructure and over 900 victim webcam videos used to impersonate victims in follow-on attacks.

incidents.victim: Government ministries (foreign affairs, defense, interior) and law enforcement agencies in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries
incidents.vector: Malicious JavaScript injected into webmail portals and government web applications compromised visitor browsers, sideloading malicious Chrome extensions via an in-browser command-and-control framework.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole passwords, emails, session cookies and communications, and used Microsoft OneDrive as a secondary command channel, consistent with strategic intelligence collection against government targets between March and May 2026; publicly disclosed Nov 11.

incidents.victim: ActiveCloud (Belarusian cloud hosting provider) and its business customers
incidents.vector: Hackers breached ActiveCloud's systems and encrypted parts of its cloud infrastructure, including its main E-Cloud hosting platform and SmartMail email service.
incidents.impact: Businesses across Belarus, including news outlet Smartpress, lost access to hosting, email and support services for several days; no evidence of customer data theft was found. Similar attacks hit Russian hosting providers ESTT (ransomware) and Beget (destructive data-wiping) in the same period.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack against Poland's national e-government services portal; technical details not yet disclosed.
incidents.impact: ePUAP was temporarily suspended, disrupting access to digital government services nationwide; Poland's digital affairs minister said evidence points to foreign-adversary involvement.

incidents.vector: Breach of FSEC systems, including the portal where financial institutions submit security assessments.
incidents.impact: Personal data was stolen from South Korea's financial-sector security regulator.

incidents.victim: Supermarkets, medical facilities, blood banks and US military commissaries (France, Belgium, Netherlands, Sweden, Luxembourg, Ireland, Estonia, US)
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to internet-exposed refrigeration controllers (likely via default credentials or unpatched software) used to force units into defrost mode or push temperatures as high as 50°C (122°F).
incidents.impact: Hundreds of supermarkets across France and over 100 additional European retail locations lost food inventory; some units overheated and caused fires. French blood bank refrigeration was also targeted but monitoring prevented spoilage. French authorities attributed the October French retail wave to the IRGC's Shahid Kaveh unit, though the November wave remains unattributed and some researchers suspect Russian hacktivist involvement (unverified claims by NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest).

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed exposed equipment following a power outage and expanded access across the port's IT network.
incidents.impact: Port operations ran on manual procedures for five days. The same port authority was separately hit by the n0n data-extortion group in October, which claimed to have stolen large volumes of data after the port refused a $26 million ransom demand.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to passport records held by Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
incidents.impact: More than 72,000 passport scans were stolen.

incidents.victim: City of Osaka, Osaka Prefecture, and ~400 Arara/TKC customers (including Sega)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached the Arara email distribution service used by TKC Corporation to administer government and corporate mailing lists.
incidents.impact: Exposed roughly 77 million email addresses across nearly 400 customers, including 1 million tied to Osaka's administrative platform; stolen addresses were used to send phishing emails impersonating financial institutions. Part of a broader surge of cyberattacks in Japan that prompted a ¥10 billion ($62 million) government emergency response package.

incidents.vector: Attackers compromised three Binance developers (via a trojanized Homebrew download and a fake job-interview coding assignment) to obtain wallet-signing privileges, then flooded a hot wallet with 50 pre-signed Ethereum EIP-7702 smart-account authorizations to install malicious 'sweeper' code.
incidents.impact: Approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency was transferred out of at least 11 Binance wallets on October 29; the malicious code kept moving funds for roughly four hours even after Binance suspended withdrawals. The FBI attributed the theft to North Korean military hackers (TraderTraitor); authorities have frozen roughly $2.85 billion, and DOJ has court authorization to seize or restrain over $1.2 billion of that amount.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS customers with internet-facing management interfaces
incidents.vector: Exploitation of PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619), two critical unauthenticated PHP remote code execution flaws, chained with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug to gain root access to exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: About 0.02% of Palo Alto Networks' installed base had internet-facing management interfaces exposed; those customers were individually contacted, and customers who applied available patches were not affected.

incidents.victim: Foreign ministries, defense, semiconductor and telecommunications organizations (200+ organizations, 14 countries)
incidents.vector: Use of the open-source agentic AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX to run automated, parallel attacks against web applications, cloud services, container environments, and mail and VPN infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Over 11 days, the actor targeted more than 200 organizations, with confirmed post-exploitation activity at nine, including extensive intrusions into two Latin American foreign ministries and a Middle East interior ministry.

incidents.vector: Following compromise of ConnectWise application credentials, used the ARTEX AI framework to accelerate automated sign-in attempts against downstream Microsoft 365 tenants.
incidents.impact: Follow-on activity involved abuse of Microsoft Graph, application credentials, and privilege changes across more than 2,250 targeted tenants.

incidents.victim: VPN appliance owners (SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet) in the US and Europe
incidents.vector: Exploited CVE-2026-0257, a Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect authentication bypass, and other VPN flaws for initial access, then deployed the newly identified GhostFrame post-exploitation framework to disable ESXi security controls, harvest credentials, and pivot across virtualized hosts.
incidents.impact: At least four victims were subsequently listed on the Settra ransomware leak site; GhostFrame gives operators centralized control over multiple virtual machines from a single compromised ESXi host.

incidents.victim: Baker Tilly (global accounting and advisory firm)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached a third-party platform used by Baker Tilly.
incidents.impact: Customer data was stolen; Baker Tilly, the world's ninth-largest accounting firm by revenue, is notifying affected customers.

incidents.victim: Semiconductor, defense and civil-society organizations (19 organizations)
incidents.vector: Used the open-source Cairn AI penetration-testing framework, paired with Chinese models Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek, to autonomously plan and execute 25 operations against 19 organizations.
incidents.impact: Achieved unauthorized access or data retrieval at 10 organizations, including over one million exposed records at a US teachers' union, persistent admin accounts at a semiconductor company, and modification of a live industry standards-ballot document.
